abstention.description: Train models to abstain when unsure (Nemotron-RL-QA-Abstention-v1, three-tier reward)
abstention.readme: This is a resources server that trains a policy model to abstain from answering when unsure rather than hallucinating. It uses a three-tier reward scheme:

aegis_v4_safety.readme: This environment uses `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Content-Safety`, also called Aegis v4, to classify a target model's prompt and response.

agentif.readme: Agentic **instruction-following** scoring, ported from THU-KEG/AgentIF (707 real-world agentic scenarios). Each row carries a list of natural-language constraints the model's response must satisfy; constraints are scored by a pipeline of typed checkers declared in the data itself.

arc_agi.readme: Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence (ARC-AGI) is a benchmark with training and evaluation data to test general reasoning. It consists of grid-based puzzles, providing a few input output pairs and the system must infer the underlying abstract transformation rule and apply it to a new input. "ARC can be seen as a general artificial intelligence benchmark, as a program synthesis benchmark, or as a psychometric intelligence test. It is targeted at both humans and artificially intelligent systems that aim at emulating a human-like form of general fluid intelligence."

arena.readme: Evaluate a model's chat capabilities on diverse conversational prompts. An LLM judge compares each response with a saved baseline in both answer orderings to reduce positional bias.

arena_judge.description: Arena Hard v2 pairwise LLM-judge (category-specific, side-swapped)
arena_judge.readme: Pairwise LLM-judge resources server implementing the arena-hard-auto judging protocol: two judge calls per rollout with swapped answer positions, category-specific prompts, and an Arena-Elo score (MLE logistic regression + 100-round bootstrap 95% CI) as the headline metric.

asr_with_pc.readme: Generic ASR / ASR-PC scoring for audio benchmarks. Reusable across benchmarks that score Word Error Rate; the LibriSpeech-PC benchmark is the first consumer, with `asr-leaderboard`, `numb3rs`, and `audiobench` as natural follow-ups.

assaybench.description: AssayBench: rank the hit genes of a CRISPR screen from its description (1,920 screens, 3 cohorts)
assaybench.verification: Adjusted nDCG@100 via the authors' `assaybench` package
assaybench.readme: AssayBench (arXiv:2605.10876, De Brouwer, Edwards et al., Genentech, May 2026) is a phenotypic-screen prediction benchmark built from 1,920 human CRISPR screens in BioGRID ORCS. Each screen is described in plain text (cell line, perturbation modality, phenotype, significance criterion, treatment) and the model must return the 100 genes most likely to be hits, ranked from strongest to weakest. The published headline is that zero-shot frontier LLMs lead (Gemini 3 Pro 0.157 AnDCG@100 on the test split), beat biology-specific models and trained predictors, and still sit far below the empirical ceiling (Oracle kNN 0.292, technical replicates roughly double the best LLM).

aviary.description: Multi-hop QA with Wikipedia search + GSM8k with calculator
aviary.readme: > Keywords: Tool Use, Multi-step Reasoning, Environment Interaction, Scientific Tasks

bbq.readme: Resources server for training LLMs to answer bias-sensitive comparative questions with evidence-grounded, stereotype-free reasoning.

bigcodebench.description: BigCodeBench Python solutions against unittest suite
bigcodebench.readme: Verifies model-generated Python solutions against the BigCodeBench unittest suite. Each task ships its own `unittest.TestCase` class plus an `entry_point` function name; the model's extracted code is calibrated (`code_prompt + "\n pass\n" + extracted`) and run through `bigcodebench.eval.untrusted_check` in an isolated subprocess.

bird_sql.description: Text-to-SQL on BIRD dev (1,534 SQLite tasks)
bird_sql.readme: Execution-based text-to-SQL verification on the BIRD dev split.

blackjack.readme: Model hits or stands using `<action>` tags until the hand ends. Game state managed per session.

browsecomp_advanced_harness.readme: RL environment for the BrowseComp benchmark — a challenging web-browsing research task requiring multi-hop investigation through search and page-level browsing.

bunsenbench_chemistry_mcq.readme: BunsenBench Chemistry MCQ verifies chemistry multiple-choice outputs for the public BunsenBench Gym benchmark. It stores materialized answer letters internally, accepts exact choice-text answers, and passes source/taxonomy metadata through to aggregate metrics.

calendar.description: Multi-turn calendar scheduling with constraint satisfaction
calendar.readme: This is a resources server for training and evaluating calendar scheduling assistants. The server verifies whether an assistant correctly schedules events with time constraints in a conversational multi-turn setting.

circle_click.readme: Environment for training VLMs to click images accurately. Uses images with colored circles on a white background and verifies that the model clicks the correct one. Image size, circle size, number of circles is configurable. Binary success reward.

circle_count.readme: Environment for training VLMs to count in images. Uses images with colored circles on a white background and verifies that the model reports the correct count for the target color. Image size, circle size, number of circles, and color distribution are configurable. Binary success reward.

citation_if.readme: A resources server that scores whether a model followed a **citation instruction**: did it cite, in the grammar it was told to use, only IDs that exist, and the ones that were required? One `/verify` endpoint, binary reward, CPU-only string matching — no model calls, no GPU.

code_fim.readme: Verifies Python code-infilling completions against the HumanEval-Infilling test suite (Bavarian et al., 2022). For each task the server splices

code_gen.readme: Verifies competitive programming solutions by executing submitted code against unit tests. The server consumes agent trajectories and returns a reward based on whether the assistant's code produces the correct outputs for given test inputs.

competitive_coding_challenges.readme: Define server-specific runtime knobs on the resource server config, then read them from `self.config` in `app.py`. For this server the relevant config path is:

conversational_tool_use_simulation.readme: This package contains the Gym environment for generated conversational tool-use tasks. Domain, policy/tool, and scenario artifacts are produced by independent Responses API agents.

critpt.description: Research-level physics problems scored by the Artificial Analysis API
critpt.readme: Evaluates research-level physics solutions on the CritPt benchmark by submitting generated code to the Artificial Analysis API.

cvdp.readme: This resources server is for model evaluation purposes. It is reproducing CVDP.

deepsearchqa.readme: Grades DeepSearchQA single-answer and set-answer responses with the official LLM judge prompt. The reward is answer-set F1: missing answers reduce recall, and unsupported extra answers reduce precision.

deepswe.readme: This resources server implements the DeepSWE v1.1 two-environment evaluation contract. The coding agent works in one sandbox; its final workspace patch is graded by the canonical DeepSWE verifier in a fresh sandbox based on the same task image.

denovo_swe.readme: Verification for AweAI-Team/DeNovoSWE, a document-to-repository training dataset: each image ships a package's source plus a written spec, and the agent must regenerate the package from the spec alone.

equivalence_llm_judge.description: Short-answer QA with LLM-as-a-judge equivalence scoring
equivalence_llm_judge.readme: Uses an LLM as a judge to compare a model’s generated answer against the expected answer.

evalplus.readme: Verifies Python function-completion benchmarks (HumanEval+, MBPP+) by running the model's extracted code against the EvalPlus base + plus test inputs. Returns two named scores per task:

example_mcp_weather.readme: A minimal example of serving a Resources Server's tools over the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**. The server is a plain `SimpleResourcesServer` with one typed HTTP tool route (`POST /get_weather`) — no MCP imports, no decorators. Setting `expose_tools_over_mcp: true` in its YAML config serves that same route over a Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint at `/mcp` on the same FastAPI app as `/seed_session` and `/verify`. Tool calls record against the per-rollout Gym session (resolved from a signed `X-NeMo-Gym-Session-Token`), and `/verify` rewards a rollout only if the tool was used **in that same session** and the final answer repeats the returned sentence.

example_multi_step.readme: The train data can be found at `example_multi_step/data/train.jsonl` and the validation data can be found at `example_multi_step/data/validation.jsonl`.

example_multi_turn_gymnasium.readme: Reference example for multi-turn environments using Gymnasium API standard.

example_session_state_mgmt.readme: This is an example environment for multi-step function calling environment. The dataset can be generated by ``` python create_examples.py ```

example_single_tool_call.readme: This is an example environment with simple tool calls. The example data can be found in `example_single_tool_call/data/example.jsonl`.

example_tool_call_multireward.readme: A single-tool-call environment that returns **multiple reward components** instead of a single scalar. This pattern is useful both for **evaluation** (profile each objective independently) and for **multi-objective RL** such as GDPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05242).

false_statement_judge.readme: Sycophancy grader: the policy is asked to *prove* a statement that is false as written, and is scored on whether it noticed — not on proof quality. Primary consumer is the `brokenarxiv` benchmark.

finance_agent_v2.readme: A NeMo Gym integration of the official Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2 that **reuses Vals's own tool code directly** (tools-only wrap) instead of reimplementing it. The upstream `finance_agent.tools.*` classes are imported and exposed as HTTP endpoints; the shared `responses_api_agents/finance_agent` loop drives them, configured to Vals's v2 harness policy in `configs/finance_agent_v2.yaml`. The public release ships no grader, so scoring is our own per-criterion rubric judge — see Verification.

finance_sec_search.description: SEC EDGAR filing search for financial analysis
finance_sec_search.readme: Financial information retrieval using SEC EDGAR filings with optional web search via Tavily.

format_verification.description: Citation format and freeform text formatting
format_verification.readme: > Keywords: Instruction Following, Format Verification, Regex, Citation, Freeform Formatting

frontierscience_judge.description: FrontierScience olympiad and research answer grading
frontierscience_judge.readme: Single-pass LLM-judge resource server for FrontierScience grading. It supports two modes:

fukuyamabench.readme: Step-by-step organic reaction-mechanism prediction. Given atom-mapped starting reactants and reaction conditions, the model predicts the full sequence of elementary steps through to the final product. Scoring is deterministic RDKit structure comparison against expert-curated mechanisms — there is no judge model anywhere in the path.

gdp_pdf.readme: GDP.pdf (Surge AI, MIT) measures professional multimodal reasoning over the documents the economy actually runs on: dense reports, contracts, filings, and records in the messy real-world formats professionals work from. The 100 prompts were written by domain experts who do this work professionally — practicing physicians, attorneys, finance professionals, engineers — across ten domains.

gdpval.readme: Scores deliverables produced by the Stirrup agent on the GDPVal benchmark.

generative_reward_model.readme: A resources server for **training** a Generative Reward Model (GenRM) with RL. Given an evaluation prompt containing conversation context and two candidate responses, the policy under training acts as the judge: it emits per-rubric and overall scores plus a relative ranking. This server parses that verdict and rewards it against human ground truth.

genrm_compare.description: GenRM pairwise comparison for RLHF training
genrm_compare.readme: A resources server that compares multiple candidate responses using a **Generative Reward Model (GenRM)** via pairwise comparisons. This module is designed for RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) training workflows, particularly for GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization).

google_search.description: MCQA with integrated Google search tool
google_search.readme: - Google Search Resources Server - Table of Contents - Description - Overview - Dataset Description - Environment Tools - Verifier - Legal Status - Requirements - Environment Inheritance - Usage Commands - Running the Server - Samples - Sample Prompts - Complete Rollout - Prompts (truncated) + Rewards - Licensing Information - Licensing information

gpqa_diamond.readme: This resources server evaluates GPQA-Diamond multiple-choice responses with a GPQA-specific verifier built on top of `resources_servers/mcqa`.

graphwalks.readme: OpenAI's GraphWalks long-context benchmark. Each task provides an adjacency list (often massive) and asks the model either to:

grl_sokoban.readme: Single-box Sokoban puzzle environment. The environment is implemented under `resources_servers/grl_sokoban/sokoban_env`, mirroring the Sokoban implementation in the GRL repo (https://github.com/lmgame-org/GRL) and based on code from https://github.com/lmgame-org/lmenv, developed in collaboration with NVIDIA. The implementation uses `gym-sokoban` (https://github.com/mpSchrader/gym-sokoban).

grl_tetris.readme: GRL Tetris environment in Gymnasium style. The model emits one or more `<action>Left|Right|Down</action>` tags per turn, the env applies them sequentially, breaking on game-over. Inner environment logic lives under `resources_servers/grl_tetris/tetris_env` and is a standalone adaptation of the upstream GRL implementation.

gui_coordinate.readme: GUI coordinate grounding verifier for visual pointing tasks. The model is shown an image and asked to point at a target; the server scores how close the predicted point is to the ground-truth coordinate.

gymnasium.readme: `GymnasiumServer` is a Gymnasium-style base class for resources servers. Implement `step()`, optionally `reset()`, and use with `gymnasium_agent`. Not a standalone server.

hotpotqa_qa.readme: Resources server for short-answer question-answering benchmarks (HotpotQA-style). Verification is fully deterministic — there is no LLM judge — and is a faithful port of the scoring used by NeMo Skills' `hotpotqa_closedbook` benchmark:

ifbench.readme: This resources server evaluates instruction following using AllenAI's IFBench library. It checks whether a model response satisfies the constraints embedded in each prompt, covering 57 distinct instruction types.

iheval.readme: IHEval is an **instruction-hierarchy** benchmark: it measures whether a model respects the priority order of system / user / tool instructions across *aligned*, *conflict*, and *reference* settings. This server ports **all** IHEval tasks and settings to NeMo Gym — including multi-turn rule-following and the reference cross-row concatenation.

image_tools.readme: PivotRL verifier for VLM image-tool trajectories. Scores a single rollout tool call against the action demonstrated at that turn in an SFT trajectory.

imo_gradingbench.readme: Four-class grading of math proofs. The policy model reads a problem statement plus a candidate proof and emits one of the words `incorrect | partial | almost | correct` as the **last word** of its response. Verification is fully deterministic — a single regex strips markdown / punctuation from the last token, lowercases it, and matches against the four-grade vocabulary — so **no external LLM judge is called**. This mirrors NeMo Skills' `gradingbench` metric type (`GradingBenchMetrics._extract_grade`).

imo_proofbench_judge.readme: LLM-judge resource server for grading IMO-style proof submissions against a reference solution and a problem-specific grading rubric.

indian_banking.readme: `indian_banking` is a multi-turn, tool-using customer-support environment for an India-based retail bank. The policy model plays the bank's virtual assistant inside an already-authenticated customer session; a second LLM plays the customer (a role-swapped user simulator driven by a per-task persona and scenario); the assistant serves the customer by calling servicing tools against a per-episode snapshot of a synthetic core-banking database, and by looking up policy in a small knowledge base. Every episode is scored once, at the end, with a dense partial-credit reward built from deterministic checks on the tool calls, the final database state, and the customer-facing messages, plus a bounded

indirect_prompt_injection.description: Resistance to injected instructions in tool-use trajectories
indirect_prompt_injection.readme: Resources server for training LLM agents to resist **indirect prompt injection** attacks during tool use.

instruction_following.readme: Evaluates language model responses against instruction-following criteria using Open-Instruct and IFEval constraints.

interactive_browser.readme: A NeMo-Gym **stateful resources server** that turns a real browser into an RL environment. Each rollout (`session_id`) owns one isolated live browser context; the policy drives it with tool calls (navigate / click / type / observe / finish); `verify()` returns the task reward from the live browser state.

inverse_if.description: Inverse instruction-following benchmark — instructions that counter conventional expectations
inverse_if.readme: Evaluates model responses on the **Inverse IF** (Instruction Following) benchmark using a per-task LLM judge. This benchmark assesses whether models can precisely follow complex, often counter-intuitive formatting and content constraints.

jailbreak_detection.readme: This resources server trains models to resist jailbreak attempts using an LLM-as-judge for verification.

job_bench.readme: Creates a sandbox per task, collects `/workspace/output` after the agent runs, and grades it with the vendored upstream Job-Bench judge (`vendor/judge.py`). Task reward is earned rubric weight divided by total rubric weight.

labbench2_vlm.description: Scientific VLM QA: figures, tables, lab protocols
labbench2_vlm.readme: Evaluates vision-language models on scientific figure and table question answering, and protocol troubleshooting, from LABBench2. For figure/table tasks the model receives a scientific figure or table alongside a free-form question. For `protocolqa2`, PDFs can be rendered as images or text-extracted via `media_mode` on the agent (see below). Verification uses an LLM-as-judge to compare the model's answer against the gold answer. Binary reward (1.0 = equivalent, 0.0 = not equivalent).

lc_niah.readme: Long-context needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) rule-based resources server for graphwalks-style tasks (BFS / parent-finding over a large directed graph). It grades a response on two signals at once:

legal_agent_bench.readme: This resource server runs the public Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) through NeMo Gym and Harbor. The integration is pinned to upstream commit `f46ef86e4788545622db25dcffa3aebb7a139929`: 1,749 tasks and the public `docx`, `pptx`, and `xlsx` skills.

litmus_agent.readme: `litmus_agent` is a **domain-agnostic** answer verifier. It extracts a value from a model response, parses that value according to the row schema, and compares it with a known answer.

longmemeval.readme: LongMemEval is a **long-term-memory QA** benchmark: each task hands the model a multi-session chat haystack and asks a question that can only be answered by recalling, reasoning over, updating or abstaining from information buried in that history. This server ports the `orig-session` / JSON-history / no-CoT configuration to NeMo Gym.

longmt_eval.readme: Document-level machine translation verifier using the SEGALE pipeline. Scores a model's translation of an entire document (book chapter, news article, or structured text) with reference-free COMETKiwi, without requiring a human reference translation.

math_advanced_calculations.readme: 1. Environment: This is a tool use - multi step agentic environment involving math problems. 2. Domain: Math 3. Example prompt: Get me the values for sin(2.0), (1.0 / 1.0), (8.0 + 3.0), (2.0 - 5.0), and (8.0 * 0.0).

math_formal_lean.readme: This environment verifies Lean4 mathematical proofs generated by language models. The model receives a theorem statement and must produce a valid proof that compiles successfully.

math_proof_judgement.description: Binary proof judgement — model reads a problem and proof, outputs Yes/No
math_proof_judgement.readme: Binary judgement of math proofs. The policy model reads a problem + candidate proof and outputs `Judgement: Yes` (proof correct) or `Judgement: No` (proof incorrect). Verification is fully deterministic — a single regex parses the final judgement — so **no external LLM judge is called**. This mirrors NeMo Skills' `answer-judgement` metric (`is_correct_judgement` format 1).

math_with_autograder.readme: Math QA resource server with a Skills-style **autograder LLM judge** as the fallback for math-verify symbolic checking. The judge is asked "is this answer Correct or Incorrect?" rather than "are these two answers equivalent?" — the prompt provides the role of grader, the model answer is the "Model Solution", and the expected answer is the "Golden Answer".

math_with_code.readme: **Environment**: Added a stateful async python code executor. The python code executor has access to scipy, numpy & pandas.

math_with_judge.readme: This is a resources server for verifying the correctness of answers to mathematical problems. It uses a combination of the Hugging Face Math-Verify library and an LLM as a judge.

mcqa.description: Multiple-choice QA covering MMLU, GPQA, HLE, LongBench
mcqa.readme: Verifies multiple-choice QA (MCQA) model outputs. It consumes agent trajectories and returns a reward based on whether the assistant’s final output matches the gold answer.

mrcr.readme: OpenAI's Multi-Round Coreference Resolution (MRCR) benchmark. Each task is a multi-turn conversation where the model has produced several outputs of the same kind (e.g. multiple poems); the final turn asks the model to reproduce the Nth occurrence exactly, prefixed by a random token.

multichallenge.description: Multi-turn inference memory and instruction retention
multichallenge.readme: Evaluates model responses on the **MultiChallenge** benchmark using an LLM judge. This benchmark assesses multi-turn conversation quality through rubric-based evaluation.

newton_bench.description: Scientific law discovery across 12 physics domains
newton_bench.readme: NeMo Gym environment for NewtonBench, to train and test LLM agents to discover scientific laws through interactive experimentation. The benchmark includes **324 scientific law discovery tasks** across **12 physics domains** (Gravitation, Electrostatics, Magnetostatics, Thermal Conduction, Geometrical Optics, Nuclear Physics, Oscillations, Physical Optics, Acoustics, Elasticity, Statistical Mechanics, Calorimetry).

ns_tools.readme: This is a resources server for executing NeMo Skills tools (e.g., stateful Python code execution) with math verification via math_with_judge.

nvarc.description: ARC-AGI in inductive (Python) and transductive (grid) modes
nvarc.readme: NVARC is an ARC-AGI style resource server with two modes: - `transductive`: the model outputs the grid directly - `inductive`: the model outputs Python code implementing `transform()`

omniscience.readme: Evaluates factual knowledge using an LLM judge on the AA-Omniscience benchmark.

openair_congestion.readme: `openair_congestion` is a multi-turn NeMo Gym environment for 5G RAN congestion control. On every turn, a policy reads cell and UE KPIs and emits exactly one of eight bounded tool calls. The resource server validates the call, the causal `replay` backend applies a deterministic synthetic transition, and the environment computes a decomposed KPI reward without an LLM judge.

openenv.description: Python code execution environment via OpenEnv
openenv.readme: Use any OpenEnv environment as a NeMo-Gym resource server. Point the adapter at an environment class via YAML config and it handles the rest -- session management, tool endpoints, reward accumulation, and verification.

osworld.readme: This Gym resources server owns stateful OSWorld `DesktopEnv` sessions and places them on a pool of remote Docker/QEMU workers. The agent and resources server may run in one deployment today, but their process and HTTP contracts remain separate:

over_refusal_detection.description: Train models to avoid refusing safe prompts

physics_judge.readme: Physics QA resource server with NeMo Skills' physics judge as the LLM-judge fallback for math-verify symbolic checking. The judge is asked "is this output correct?" and emits `[Correct]` / `[Incorrect]` verdict tokens.

polymath.description: Multilingual math across 18 languages and 4 difficulty tiers
polymath.readme: Verifies multilingual math answers from the PolyMath benchmark and reports difficulty-weighted, per-language metrics.

proof_genselect.readme: This environment presents a math problem together with two candidate proofs and asks the model to choose the better one.

proof_judge.readme: This environment trains or evaluates theorem-proving models that produce both a solution and a self-evaluation.

proof_verification.readme: This environment scores a model that evaluates the quality of a proof or solution. The policy is given a problem, a candidate proof, and instructions to write a detailed evaluation ending with a boxed score in `{0, 0.5, 1}`.

ragtruth.readme: Case-level **hallucination detection** over the `qa` / `summary` / `data2txt` slices. The model is shown a `(reference context, candidate response)` pair and must emit a `{"hallucination list": [...]}` JSON object listing any hallucinated spans. The per-sample reward is `1.0` when the model's binary "any hallucination?" verdict matches the gold label, else `0.0`.

reasoning_gym.description: 100+ tasks: algebra, logic, geometry, graph theory, games

rolemrc.readme: Role-play machine-reading-comprehension scoring. The model plays a character and answers questions about supplied passages while respecting the character's knowledge range, speech style, and instruction priority.

ruler2.readme: Verifier for the RULER v2 long-context benchmark suite. Ports the verification logic from `nemo_skills.evaluation.evaluator.ruler.eval_ruler2` and the multichoice extractor from `nemo_skills.evaluation.evaluator.mcq.eval_mcq`.

scale_swe.readme: Verification for AweAI-Team/Scale-SWE: 20,181 software-engineering tasks, entirely Python.

scicode.readme: Verifies multi-step scientific code generation on the SciCode benchmark. The agent submits the code it generated for each sub-step; this server executes each sub-step's accumulated code against ground-truth targets in `test_data.h5` and returns the reward.

scicodepile.readme: Verifies Python solutions against the executable stratum of SciCodePile, a corpus and benchmark for scientific code generation built from 37,737 public computational-science repositories. This server covers the **runnable benchmark** — 200 tasks, each shipping its own test — not the corpus's completion/infilling tasks.

sec_local_index.readme: Shared SEC search code. This is a library, not a resources server: nothing starts it, and `entrypoint: local_edgar_search.py` in its config exists only because every module under `resources_servers/` declares one, the same way `resources_servers/gymnasium` does. `data/` holds the five smoke rows the module test gate requires; no agent runs them. Two servers import this package.

simpleqa.description: Short-form factual QA with abstention scoring
simpleqa.readme: Evaluates short-form factual QA using an LLM judge that grades on a 3-tier scale (CORRECT / INCORRECT / NOT_ATTEMPTED). Mirrors the SimpleQA-Verified judge protocol.

single_step_tool_use_with_argument_compa.description: Pivot RL for tool use across conversational, SWE, and search domains
single_step_tool_use_with_argument_compa.readme: This is a resources server that is to be used to verify a single action taken by an agent that can either call a tool or send a chat message to the user as the next step in a trajectory. For each verification request, there is an expected action that is either a tool call or a chat message. An expected tool call is compared with a tool call issued by the agent by programmatically comparing the arguments in the tool calls. If the expected action is a chat message, then the agent receives a positive reward if it sends a chat message, and a negative reward if it calls a tool instead.

spartqa.readme: Spatial-reasoning benchmark covering SpartQA's **CO (choose-object)** question type. The model is shown a story, a question of the form "… X or Y?", and four candidate answers; it must copy one of them, ending with a `Final answer: <candidate answer>` line. The per-sample reward is `1.0` iff the answer resolves to the gold label, else `0.0`.

speed_bench.readme: Speculative-decoding throughput resources server. Reads vLLM's Prometheus `/metrics` counters before and after generation to compute **acceptance length (AL)** and **acceptance rate (AR)** across the benchmark window. Ported from `nemo_skills/inference/eval/specdec.py`.

spider2_lite.readme: Execution-based text-to-SQL evaluation on Spider 2.0-Lite, a real-world enterprise SQL benchmark. Binary reward: 1.0 if the predicted SQL produces a result set equivalent to the gold, 0.0 otherwise. No LLM judge required.

string_match.readme: General-purpose string matching verifier for free-form text answers. It pulls a candidate answer out of the model response, then compares it to `expected_answer` with the NeMo RL string-match grader (no format reward).

structeval.description: StructEval: JSON, YAML, CSV, TOML, XML schema adherence
structeval.readme: > Keywords: Instruction Following, Structured Outputs, StructEval, Code Generation

structured_outputs.description: Schema adherence across structured output formats
structured_outputs.readme: > Keywords: Instruction Following, Structured Outputs, Schema Adherence

swe_internal_v1.readme: Verification for the internal-v1 SWE delivery: real GitHub PRs turned into software-engineering tasks (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, a few C++ repositories), each with its own prebuilt image, a hidden test patch, a golden patch, and a vendor-authored test runner + output parser pair.

swe_next.readme: Verification for TIGER-Lab/SWE-Next: Python software-engineering tasks generated by the R2E ("Repo-to-Environment") pipeline.

swe_pivot.readme: Verifier for PivotRL training on coding agent trajectories. Scores rollout actions at pivot turns — critical decision points where the model's choice determines fix success or failure.

swe_rebench.readme: Verification for nebius/SWE-rebench-V2: 32,079 software-engineering tasks across 20 languages.

swebench.readme: In a separate terminal: ```bash gym eval prepare --config benchmarks/swebench/verified/opencode.yaml

swebench_pro.readme: This resources server evaluates patches for the public ScaleAI SWE-bench Pro benchmark with NeMo Gym `AsyncSandbox` providers.

swemer_oml.readme: Verification for the OML SWE-bench Extended delivery: 5,000 real GitHub PRs turned into software-engineering tasks (Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, C/C++), each with its own prebuilt image, a hidden test patch, a golden patch, and, unlike the Swemer deliveries, its own grader.

swemer_v1.readme: Verification for Swemer's Agentic-v1 SWE task packages: real GitHub PRs turned into software-engineering tasks, each with its own prebuilt image, held-out tests, and a golden patch.

swemer_v2.readme: Verification for Swemer's Agentic-v2 SWE task packages: real GitHub PRs turned into software-engineering tasks, each with its own prebuilt image, held-out tests, and a golden patch.

swerl_gen.description: SWE patch and test generation in a sandboxed environment
swerl_gen.readme: Generates patches or reproduction tests and evaluates them in a sandbox environment. It gets agent candidate patches/tests and returns a reward. In the case of patch generation, it uses PASS_TO_PASS and FAIL_TO_PASS tests (as defined by SWE-bench) for evaluation. When a reproduction test is generated, it checks whether the test reports `issue reproduced` (exit code 2) before applying the patch and `issue solved` (exit code 0) after applying the patch.

swerl_llm_judge.readme: Verifies LLM-as-a-judge capability of models for software engineering tasks. It consumes agent candidated patches and returns a reward based on whether the assistant’s final output matches the gold answer.

toolsandbox.readme: Multi-turn, stateful, tool-using benchmark ported from apple/ToolSandbox. An agent-under-test (the gym policy model) converses with a simulated user while issuing Python tool calls against a stateful sandbox (contacts, messaging, reminders, device settings). Each scenario is scored against milestone / minefield snapshots; the reward is the milestone **similarity** in `[0, 1]` (0 if a minefield is hit).

vibench.readme: ViBench evaluates whether a model can build a working web application from a product requirements document. A task hands the agent a PRD and an empty container; grading stands the finished app up for real, seeds it with data through its own UI, and then drives it in a browser against a human-written test plan.

wmt_translation.description: Machine translation with BLEU and xCOMET-XXL
wmt_translation.readme: Generic machine-translation verifier for WMT-style benchmarks. Computes corpus-level spBLEU and chrF per `(source_language, target_language)` pair via sacrebleu. spBLEU always uses SacreBLEU's `flores200` SentencePiece tokenizer, regardless of the target language. Optionally augments them with xCOMET-XXL neural QE scores, served by a persistent Ray actor pool that loads the checkpoint once per actor and stays resident for the whole run, plus optional language-consistency scoring through a configured backend.

agent_types.anyswe_agent: AnySWE runs a Gym agent inside a SWE task image, extracts its repository patch, and grades the patch in a fresh OpenSandbox environment. It supports SWE-bench, SWE-bench Multilingual, and R2E-Gym.
agent_types.anyterminal_agent: Runs any Gym agent inside a Terminal Bench task container and evaluates the result by running the task's `tests/test.sh` in the same container. Works with `hermes_agent`, `claude_code_agent`, `terminus_2_agent`, or any other compatible Gym agent.
agent_types.aviary_agent: Aviary is a framework built by FutureHouse for developing tools and environments for LLM agents. This integration allows NeMo Gym rollouts over Aviary environments and datasets.
agent_types.claude_code_agent: Runs Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`) as a NeMo Gym agent server.
agent_types.cline_agent: Runs the Cline CLI headlessly (`cline --json`). Cline runs its own tools internally, and its newline-delimited JSON event stream is parsed into Gym format and verified by the resources server.
agent_types.codex_agent: Runs the OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex exec`) as a NeMo Gym agent server.
agent_types.conversational_tool_use: The conversational tool-use workflow is implemented by four Responses API agents:
agent_types.critpt_agent: Custom two-turn agent for the CritPt benchmark (research-level physics problems). For each problem it:
agent_types.cvdp_agent: Agents for the **CVDP** (Comprehensive Verilog Design Problems) benchmark — hardware (RTL/SystemVerilog) design and code-comprehension tasks. All flavors here share the same CVDP resources server, which owns task data, verification, and reward computation. See `resources_servers/cvdp/` for benchmark details.
agent_types.finance_agent: Multi-turn tool-calling loop for the Vals AI finance agent benchmarks. Two server instances configure it, and they are the only difference between the two harnesses — the loop itself has no benchmark-specific branches.
agent_types.gdp_pdf_agent: A thin `simple_agent` subclass that embeds a pre-rendered document into the model request at rollout time, with a reactive DPI backoff for policy models that reject or truncate oversized requests.
agent_types.gymnasium_agent: Agent for Gymnasium-style environments based on `GymnasiumServer` resources servers. Drives the reset/step loop.
agent_types.harbor_agent: This agent integrates Harbor into NeMo Gym. It runs Harbor agents (e.g., `terminus-2`) in Harbor-managed environments and returns NeMo Gym-compatible outputs.
agent_types.harbor_agent_general: This agent integrates the Harbor Framework into NeMo Gym. The rollouts are compeletely owned by Harbor and NeMo Gym acts as the orchestrator, converting the Agent Trajectory Format (ATIF) to NeMo Gym-compatible outputs. Harbor-related configuration is transparently exposed for use in a NeMo Gym configuration file, allowing easy translation from `harbor run` commands.
agent_types.harness_agent: Runs any gym agent harness in a sandbox with any resources server.
agent_types.harness_exa_search: Runs a Gym agent harness in a sandbox with Exa search, then delegates grading to the configured resources server. Benchmark-local configs are available for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, OpenClaw, Kilocode, Cline, Prime Agent, Simple Strands, and NeMo Fabric DeepAgents. Validation depth varies by harness, so use a one-task smoke test before a full run.
agent_types.haystack_agent: A NeMo Gym agent harness that runs a serialized Haystack `Pipeline` as its rollout loop. The pipeline contains a Haystack `Agent` whose `chat_generator` is a `NeMoGymResponsesChatGenerator` — a Haystack `ChatGenerator` that calls a native NeMo Gym model server's `/v1/responses` endpoint (resolved by `server_name`). Haystack's `Agent` drives the repeated tool-calling loop. It can use Haystack-local tools, request-supplied HTTP environment tools, and `ContextAwareMCPToolset` environment tools exposed over MCP.
agent_types.hermes_sandboxed_agent: Runs **NousResearch/hermes-agent** inside the task container prepared by Gym's existing SWE-bench Pro resources server. Hermes uses its terminal and file tools in `/app`; Pro extracts and grades the patch through its existing verifier. The model server runs separately. See ASSESSMENT.md for the component map and code review order.
agent_types.image_tools_agent: The image tools agent adds iterative image inspection to an existing NeMo Gym agent workflow. It sends each request to the configured model, executes supported image tool calls, and returns the final assistant response to the resource server for verification.
agent_types.kilocode_agent: Runs the Kilo Code CLI (`kilo run`). Kilo Code is a fork of OpenCode, so this agent mirrors the `opencode_agent`: Kilo runs its own tools internally, and its JSON event stream (`--format json`) is parsed into Gym format and verified by the resources server.
agent_types.labbench2_vlm_agent: Custom agent extending `simple_agent` for the `labbench2_vlm` resource server.
agent_types.langchain_deepagents_agent: Runs a LangChain DeepAgents agent as a native NeMo Gym agent server.
agent_types.langgraph_agent: Examples here include a iterative reflection agent, subagent orchestrator agent, parallel thinking agent, and rewoo agent. Most of these are based on langgraph examples: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/tree/main/examples
agent_types.mini_swe_agent: A NeMo Gym responses API agent that integrates the Mini-SWE-Agent harness for evaluating language models on software engineering tasks using the SWE-Bench dataset.
agent_types.mini_swe_agent_2: A NeMo Gym Responses API agent that integrates mini-swe-agent v2 for evaluating language models on SWE-bench style software engineering tasks through the public `nemo_gym.sandbox` API.
agent_types.miniswe_sandboxed_agent: Run pinned mini-SWE 2.4.6 directly in a resource-owned Linux sandbox, using its native CLI, `DefaultAgent`, `LocalEnvironment`, and `litellm_response` model. Use the TB4 profile with TB4 resources.
agent_types.nemo_fabric_agent: Run interchangeable agent harnesses through NeMo Fabric inside NeMo Gym.
agent_types.non_executing_simple_agent: This agent forwards a single `/v1/responses` request to the configured model server and passes the model response directly to the configured resource server verifier.
agent_types.nooa_agent: The NOOA agent adapter provides typed configuration for constructing NOOA agents and invoking them through asynchronous Python adapters that receive validated NeMo Gym Responses requests.
agent_types.openclaw_agent: Runs OpenClaw CLI (`openclaw agent --local --json`). OpenClaw runs its own tools internally. Resources server is used for verifier.
agent_types.opencode_agent: Runs the OpenCode CLI (`opencode run`). OpenCode runs its own tools internally. The run's sqlite session is read for the full trajectory (including tool calls) and converts it into Gym format and uses resources server to verify.
agent_types.osworld_agent: The OSWorld agent runs complete desktop-computer tasks through NeMo Gym. The agent and benchmark stay in the Gym process; only the OSWorld desktop container/VM lifecycle moves into Gym Docker Sandbox. Each `/run` request creates an OSWorld `DesktopEnv`, sends observations to the configured model, parses and executes actions, invokes OSWorld's inline evaluator, and returns the trajectory and reward in Gym's Responses API shape.
agent_types.pi_agent: Runs the pi CLI (`pi --print --mode json --no-session`). pi runs its own tools internally. Resources server for verifier.
agent_types.pi_sandboxed_agent: Runs the native Pi CLI inside a provider-managed sandbox, with Gym handling model requests, MCP tools, transcript export, and verification.
agent_types.pinchbench: PinchBench measures how well an LLM performs as the **brain of an OpenClaw agent** across 147 real-world tasks (calendar, email triage, CSV/log analysis, coding, research, writing). Each task is graded by deterministic checks, an LLM judge, or both.
agent_types.prime_agent: Runs Prime Agent in headless JSON mode.
agent_types.proof_refinement_agent: Multi-turn self-correction agent for formal proof verification.
agent_types.remote_agent: An agent server that drives an agent service you host yourself — in your own repo, on your own infrastructure. Your service implements one endpoint **compliant with the OpenAI `/v1/responses` contract**, and the two servers compose as Responses-speaking agents: each call your service receives the conversation so far and returns what it wants to do next. Gym runs the loop.
agent_types.scicode_agent: Custom multi-step agent for the SciCode benchmark. For each problem it loops over the sub-steps, generating Python code one sub-step at a time and accumulating it (each sub-step's prompt includes the model's own code from previous sub-steps), then submits the accumulated per-step solutions to the SciCode resources server's `/verify` for execution.
agent_types.simple_agent_with_compaction: This Responses API agent follows the same model/tool rollout loop as `simple_agent`, while maintaining a semantic history that can be materialized through a configured context-compaction policy before each model call.
agent_types.simple_strands_agent: The pinned Simple Strands Agent dependency is installed with the agent server. The native system prompt is retained and additional system prompts are appended.
agent_types.speed_bench_agent: NeMo-Gym's `simple_agent` performs at most one model call per task: given `responses_create_params.input = [user_1, user_2, ...]`, it sends the entire message list to the model in a single `/v1/responses` call.
agent_types.stirrup_agent: A NeMo Gym responses API agent that uses the Stirrup agent-loop framework to evaluate language models on GDPVal — a benchmark of real-world professional knowledge-work tasks across sectors like finance, law, healthcare, and engineering.
agent_types.swe_agents: A unified Responses-API wrapper that runs LLM-driven agents against real-world software-engineering benchmarks (SWE-bench and friends), executes the proposed patch inside the dataset's evaluation harness, and returns trajectories + a binary "resolved" reward suitable for both evaluation and RL training.
agent_types.tau2: The banking_knowledge configs use the Tau2 bridge with Tau3 data and retrieval configuration in the prepared rows:
agent_types.terminus_2_agent: Runs Harbor's Terminus-2 as a NeMo Gym Responses API agent.
agent_types.terminus_2_sandboxed_agent: This agent runs Harbor's `Terminus2` control loop in the task sandbox supplied by the NeMo Gym resources server. It adapts the small Harbor environment interface that Terminus uses (`exec` and `is_dir`) to `AsyncSandbox`; task state therefore remains owned by the resources server.
agent_types.tool_simulation_agent: This is a responses API agent that is intended to be used when any required tool execution results are generated by simulation.
agent_types.toolsandbox_agent: Agent harness for the ToolSandbox multi-turn tool-use benchmark. It is a thin fork of `aviary_agent`: ToolSandbox is a conversation, not a pure tool loop, so when the policy model replies in natural language (no tool calls) that reply is forwarded to the **user simulator** and the episode continues, rather than ending the rollout on a no-tool-call turn.
agent_types.vcqa_agent: Verified Code QA (VCQA) evaluates code-investigation ability on real GitHub repositories. Each task gives the model a problem statement plus a per-task working tree: either a repository snapshot tarball or a git bundle checked out at a target commit. The agent exposes read-only file tools and sandboxed `bash`, then grades the final assistant answer with an LLM judge against the task's must-have rubric.
agent_types.verifiers_agent: This agent enables running Prime Intellect verifiers environments, including many in Prime Intellect's Environments Hub in NeMo Gym.
agent_types.vibench_agent: The build half of the ViBench environment. It takes a product requirements document, builds a working web application in its own sandbox, and copies the result out as a tarball for `resources_servers/vibench` to stand up and grade.
